judged_text: This block adds an unconditional Salesforce token refresh (remote POST + credential DB write) on the connection-creation path that previously served directly from cached credentialKey, plus a hardcoded login.salesforce.com URL and a dead `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check (parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure). Every Salesforce calendar operation pays an extra token-endpoint round-trip and a DB write per connection creation, a hot-path regression unrelated to the stated credential-sync objective that entered the PR without its own acceptance; the hardcoded URL also ignores instance_url for custom Salesforce domains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SalesforceCalendarService now unconditionally performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately persists the result via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (see added block in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`). This means connection creation now always incurs a network round-trip and DB write, which is a concrete hot-path/performance/architecture concern (even if it may still work correctly). The finding’s note about a dead check is also grounded: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` throws on `!success`, so the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is effectively unreachable. The “hardcoded URL ignores instance_url/custom domains” is a reasonable concern because the endpoint is fixed in code and does not reference any previously stored domain/instance value, though actual correctness impact can’t be fully proven from the diff alone.
